text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between West Ham and Newcastle United at London Stadium!

Making it three straight wins in three different competitions, West Ham's most recent victory came on Thursday, as the Europa Conference League champions beat Bundesliga side Freiburg 2-1 in the Europa League.
Last weekend, the Hammers saw off struggling Sheffield United with a 2-0 Premier League win, and they occupy seventh place in the table with seven matches played.
However, ahead of today's game, the London club have won just one of their last eight league meetings with Newcastle United.
Newcastle arrive in the capital having stunned Europe with their 4-1 thumping of Paris Saint-Germain in midweek.

Following the Magpies' biggest-ever victory in the Champions League group stages - plus a recent 8-0 thrashing of Sheffield United, an EFL Cup success over Manchester City and a 2-0 Premier League defeat of Burnley - they now seek their fifth straight win in all competitions.
Such a result would help Eddie Howe's men leapfrog West Ham in the table.
In their final fixture before the upcoming international break, West Ham make five changes to the team that won in Germany last time out.
Most notably, Antonio returns from injury to start up front, captain Zouma is selected at the back, and Areola replaces Fabianski in goal.
Newcastle also have one of their main marksmen back in the fold today, as Antonio's good friend Wilson returns from a thigh problem and starts on the bench.
Lascelles continues to deputise for Botman after captaining the Magpies on Wednesday.
Meanwhile, Anthony Gordon has already accumulated five Premier League yellow cards so serves a suspension; Anderson replaces him.
The players are out on the pitch at a sunny London Stadium, and kick-off is now just moments away!
The hosts kick off, and we are under way in London!
Bowen and Soucek combine on the right, but Newcastle's defence quickly close them both down to nip any potential danger in the bud.
Otherwise, the visitors have had more of the ball so far.
Trippier floats over a cross from the right, but as Anderson attempts to meet it at the back post, he comes under intense pressure from Coufal and can only steer his header off target.
West Ham may have scored in all of their Premier League home games throughout 2023 so far, but not since March 2019 have they managed to defeat Newcastle in front of their own supporters.
Can they end that barren run today?
Burn forces Bowen to concede a throw-in near the touchline, as Newcastle continue to impose themselves on the home side, who are yet to find any rhythm.

WEST HAM LEAD! Against the early run of play, the Hammers go 1-0 in front! Paqueta flicks a lovely ball over the top for Emerson to gather near the left byline, and the full-back then plays a low pass inside to Soucek, who beats a flailing Pope and calmly finds the bottom-right corner!
Taking Paqueta's lofted pass into his stride, Emerson cuts the ball back from the left byline and sets up Soucek's goal.
With Soucek's third goal in eight Premier League appearances against Newcastle, West Ham have now scored in 10 successive top-flight games.
What a start for the home side!
Despite falling behind, Newcastle have resumed their patient passing approach - there's no sign of panic.
The goal came out of the blue, really, and it had been an encouraging start for Howe's men until that point.
West Ham have had just 26 per cent of possession so far, and they are sitting inside their own half, aiming to frustrate Newcastle and pounce on the break.
It's an approach that's already borne fruit today.
Anderson sends a throughball straight out of play, much to the home fans' delight, and Newcastle are yet to force a significant opening in West Ham's defence.
Having gestured towards the referee, asking for his opponent to be shown a yellow card, Emerson joins Bruno Guimaraes in the referee's notebook.
A clear trip on Emerson results in Bruno Guimaraes receiving the first yellow card of the game.
After making another potentially bookable challenge and conceding a free-kick, Bruno Guimaraes is perhaps fortunate not to see a second yellow card in the space of a few minutes.
A long chat with the referee lets him know that's his last warning.
Suddenly afforded some space, Paqueta drills a low ball across from the left side of the box, but Schar intervenes and Newcastle manage to get the ball clear.
Longstaff is caught narrowly offside when receiving a throughball from Trippier on the right flank, ending another unconvincing Newcastle attack: they've yet to find any fluency in the final third.
After Burn nods a dangerous cross behind for a corner, Ward-Prowse delivers an inswinging cross.
Pope punches it clear from inside his six-yard box, then the whistle blows for a foul on the goalkeeper by Antonio.
Due to an alert sprint from the goal-line by Pope, Antonio can't quite connect with a ball into the box.
Newcastle's number one claims it and snuffs out the danger.
CLOSE! Tonali drives forward and then feeds Almiron out on the right.
Although faced with a difficult angle and still nearly 25 yards from goal, the Paraguayan lets fly with a powerful shot that zips narrowly wide of the left-hand post!
Badly mistiming his tackle, Paqueta brings down Lascelles midway through West Ham's half and concedes a free-kick out on the right.

JUST WIDE! Flicking a header just past the left-hand post from inside the box, Burn comes close for Newcastle! As ever, Trippier's set-piece delivery from the right picks out a runner, but the full-back can't quite apply the right finish.
From a deep free-kick, Zouma launches a long ball towards the Newcastle area, but the visitors easily mop it up and that was a waste of possession.
For halting Isak's speedy run with a crude challenge, Antonio becomes the latest player booked by the referee.
There have been plenty of tackles flying in so far today.
Having failed to test Pope since going one goal ahead, it has been 30 minutes since West Ham last attempted a shot.
Their latest attack sees Antonio flagged for offside as he seeks to meet Paqueta's throughball.
Crossed wires between Areola and Zouma result in the latter hacking the ball clear from near his goal-line following Tonali's cross.
It was perhaps a bit panicky, but at least got the job done.
Picking up the ball from Trippier on the right side of the box, Bruno Guimaraes looks up and aims to pick out a team-mate at the back post.
However, his pass is overhit and sails straight out of play - he then raises his hand by way of apology.
Trippier fells Antonio midway through West Ham's half, but the referee declines to issue a yellow card.
It's been a frustrating first half for Newcastle so far, and they don't really look much like scoring.
As a minimum of two minutes stoppage time are announced, neither side seem any closer to adding to the only shot on target we've had at London Stadium today - Soucek's early goal.
HALF-TIME: WEST HAM 1-0 NEWCASTLE UNITED
Having soaked up some early pressure and then clinically struck on the counter, West Ham have been content to sit in and defend their lead, which sees them lead Newcastle United at the break.
Despite having less than 30 per cent possession, the Hammers have controlled events with their disciplined defensive shape, and it's been a David Moyes masterclass so far.
Newcastle, meanwhile, are perhaps suffering a Champions League hangover, as they've lacked fluency and are yet to record a single shot on target.
West Ham have now stopped the opposition from scoring a first-half goal in six of their eight Premier League games this season - only Crystal Palace and Wolves have done so more often.
Also with a record of three wins from four when leading at half-time, the Hammers are in a great position at the break.
Newcastle kick off, and we are back under way at London Stadium!
Some 21 goals have been scored across the last five editions of this fixture, five of which went to Newcastle in a 5-1 win here back in April.
Events so far today don't suggest that tradition will continue - there's been no goalmouth action as yet in the second half.
A delicious first-time pass by Paqueta splits Newcastle's centre-backs, but just as Bowen is set to pounce, Burn intervenes and turns the ball behind for a corner.

MISS! Spurning a great chance to extend West Ham's lead, Alvarez nods wide from close range! The midfielder dives down to meet a Ward-Prowse cross, but his diving header spins just wide of the left-hand post!
Almiron surges to the right byline, causing a moment of concern in West Ham's massed defence, but he then overruns the ball and it trickles behind for a goal-kick to West Ham.
Newcastle are applying some sustained pressure now, as West Ham resume their deep defensive line.
Will this approach get the home side over the line, or can the Magpies eventually break through?
SUPER SAVE! Areola dives down low to keep out Burn's close-range header, following a clever stood-up cross by Isak from the right! Great goalkeeping, but what a chance missed!

NEWCASTLE ARE LEVEL! After Trippier sends a free-kick into the box from deep, Isak benefits from a deflection off Alvarez and sweeps the ball past Areola and into the top of the net! It's 1-1 at London Stadium, and Newcastle's pressure has paid off!
GOAL STANDS! Isak faced a worrying wait as the VAR analysed his goal for a possible offside, but as the ball came off a West Ham player before he steered it in, the Swedish striker was onside.

ISAK STRIKES AGAIN! Another Trippier delivery sets up Isak to put Newcastle in front! A volleyed pass from the right byline perfectly picks out the Magpies main man up front, leaving a simple task to turn the ball in from close range! All of a sudden, it's 2-1 to Newcastle - how will West Ham respond?
Cushioning a superb volleyed cross towards Isak in the six-yard box, Trippier adds another assist to his lengthy list.
Trippier has provided more assists (12) and created more chances than any other Premier League defender since the start of last season.
His five assists so far this term have come in his last three league games.
Arriving at the back post, Anderson meets a cross from Trippier, but Coufal intervenes and does just enough to stop the Newcastle man striking cleanly at goal.
It's still all Newcastle.
After blocking Aguerd's attempt to take a defensive free-kick, Almiron picks up a booking.
Burn steals the ball from Antonio deep in Newcastle territory, and despite the home fans' calls for a free-kick, play continues.
West Ham continue to lack teeth in attack, so surely Moyes will make some changes soon.
Paqueta is shown a yellow card for vociferously demanding that Antonio was fouled by Burn.
Unexpectedly, set-piece specialist Ward-Prowse plays a free-kick short to Coufal just inside Newcastle's half, but the latter's high ball into the box is easily gathered by Pope.
OFF THE POST! Isak just misses out on a hat-trick! Receiving the ball on the edge of the box, he sits down Areola with some silky skill and then shoots from a tight angle on the right.
However, it bounces back off the near post and then hits Aguerd, resulting in a Newcastle corner.
Moyes makes his move: having just returned from injury, Antonio cannot complete the game, so Benrahma replaces him.
Opening goalscorer Soucek also departs, as Kudus comes on to add some more variety in attack.
A clash of shins between Longstaff and Emerson leaves both men down on the turf.
After a brief pause in proceedings, though, the action can resume - and Ward-Prowse will have a good chance to shoot from a 20-yard free-kick.
For delaying West Ham's free-kick by moving forward from the defensive wall, Longstaff joins the list of players booked today.

CLOSE! With a whipped free-kick from just outside the area, Ward-Prowse sends the ball curling narrowly over the crossbar! He was perhaps a little too close to get it up and down in time to hit the target, but it was a typically good attempt.
Another energetic shift from Almiron is brought to its end, as Howe sends on Murphy to add fresh legs to Newcastle's front line.
For the first time today, West Ham are pressing forward with purpose, and their substitutions seem to have livened up a moribund attack.
However, after failing to make the most of a corner, they then see Paqueta's chipped throughball drift straight through to Pope.
Having come so close to a second-half hat-trick, Isak departs with two game-changing goals to his name.
Wilson completes his return from injury by arriving off the bench.
Just introduced to the action, Wilson loves playing West Ham: he has scored more Premier League goals against them than against any other opponent, netting 12 times in 13 previous appearances.
Only Wayne Rooney (14) and Michael Owen (13) have scored more often against the Hammers in England's top flight.

WEST HAM PULL LEVEL! After Coufal sprints down the right and cuts back a sharp ball inside, Kudus takes one touch to set himself and then lashes a low left-footed strike into the bottom corner! Pope had no chance, and that's quite a way to score his first Premier League goal: 2-2!

text: Summoning up one last surge of energy to burst down the right, Coufal then coolly pulls the ball back for Kudus, who hauls the Hammers level.

SHARP STOP! Pope keeps his side level! Bowen cuts in from the right, then drives a low shot towards the far post, forcing Newcastle's goalkeeper to dive full length and tip the ball wide! Benrahma fails to make contact with the rebound, so it's just a corner-kick.
Howe decides to stiffen things up out wide, so Anderson is withdrawn and a full-back, Targett, is sent on.
In the fifth minute of at least six added for stoppages, West Ham continue to push for a late winner.
What a turnaround at London Stadium - they'd barely ventured into Newcastle's defensive third before going 2-1 down!
Trippier hangs up a free-kick from the right touchline towards Lascelles, but the Newcastle captain's header is then swallowed up in a packed penalty area.
West Ham ultimately get the ball clear, and it seems it'll be one point apiece.
FULL-TIME: WEST HAM 2-2 NEWCASTLE UNITED

Despite dominating the ball and improving offensively after a barren first half, Newcastle United can't follow up their landmark win over PSG with another Premier League victory, as West Ham snatch a late leveller.

Isak's clinical finishing earned the Magpies a 2-1 lead heading into the closing stages, but substitute Kudus struck a superb equaliser with time running out and the spoils are shared at London Stadium.
All things considered, perhaps that's the fairest outcome.

West Ham still lead Newcastle by a point going into the international break, after which the Hammers will visit Aston Villa for an all claret-and-blue clash in Birmingham; meanwhile, Newcastle next host Crystal Palace and then Champions League opponents Borussia Dortmund.
That's all from London Stadium today, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!
